extracted.intended_audience: Established basic and biomedical researchers (faculty-level) considering applying to the HHMI Investigator competition
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines and eligibility/selection criteria for applying to HHMI’s Investigator Program, including required applicant qualifications, application components, institutional commitments, and expectations for appointees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Degree requirement
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is stated as a general eligibility requirement for applicants to the Investigator program.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research time commitment
rubrics_metrics.description: Plan to dedicate at least 75% of their time to research at an eligible US institution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants must commit the majority of their professional time (≥75%) to research at an institution that meets HHMI's eligibility criteria.

rubrics_metrics.name: Institutional position requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Hold a position that represents substantial commitment by their institution, such as a tenure-track faculty position.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants must occupy a role at their host institution that demonstrates institutional support and commitment (examples include tenure-track faculty positions).

rubrics_metrics.name: Track record of peer-reviewed funding
rubrics_metrics.description: Have a track record of peer-reviewed funding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prior success in obtaining peer-reviewed research funding is required evidence of an applicant's ability to secure and manage research support.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required post-training/professional experience
rubrics_metrics.description: Meet the required length of post-training, professional experience prior to applying.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The program requires applicants to have a specified amount of post-training/professional experience (the page notes this requirement though the exact length is provided in application materials).

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligible fields/disciplines
rubrics_metrics.description: Investigator competitions are open to researchers in basic and biomedical sciences, plant biology, evolutionary biology, biophysics, chemical biology, biomedical engineering, and computational biology.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants must be working in one of the listed disciplines to be eligible for the competition.

rubrics_metrics.name: ORCID and ARC eligibility check
rubrics_metrics.description: To determine eligibility to apply to the competition, log in to HHMI’s Application and Review Channel (ARC), or register if first-time user; to register you must have an ORCID identifier (ORCID iD).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ARC performs an immediate eligibility check when applicants submit required information and acknowledge appointment conditions; having an ORCID iD is a prerequisite to register.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application component — five scientific contributions
rubrics_metrics.description: Application requirements include a description of five distinct scientific research contributions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants must succinctly describe five separate contributions to science; the program announcement and ARC provide the formatting and bibliography template to follow.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application component — program description
rubrics_metrics.description: Program description focused on your ongoing and planned research program.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants must provide a description concentrating on both current work and planned future research directions, consistent with HHMI's 'people, not projects' approach.

rubrics_metrics.name: Follow formatting and bibliography templates
rubrics_metrics.description: The application includes formatting guidelines and the required bibliography template which applicants must follow.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ARC and the program announcement supply specific formatting instructions and a bibliography template — applicants are expected to adhere to these materials when preparing submissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection based on scientific assessment
rubrics_metrics.description: HHMI’s scientific leadership selects Investigators based on assessment by a panel of distinguished scientists, including members of HHMI advisory boards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Selection emphasizes evaluation by peers and leaders in the field; the program values researchers who 'break new ground' and whose work can 'radically change our understanding' of biology. This implies assessment of scientific excellence, originality, and impact potential.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expectation of transformative, boundary‑pushing research
rubrics_metrics.description: Investigators are expected to do research that radically changes our understanding of how biology works.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: HHMI prioritizes transformative breakthroughs and supports 'talented scientists' with freedom to pursue bold ideas — applicants should demonstrate evidence of high-impact, innovative contributions and future potential.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appointment term and renewal process
rubrics_metrics.description: Investigators are appointed to a seven-year renewable term; renewal decisions are made by HHMI scientific leadership based on assessment and review by a panel of distinguished scientists.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appointment is not indefinite; continuation beyond seven years depends on subsequent review and demonstrated continuing excellence and productivity as assessed by HHMI’s review process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Institutional agreement and concurrent appointment
rubrics_metrics.description: Appointments involve a collaborative agreement between HHMI and the Investigator’s host institution, where the Investigator holds a concurrent appointment and maintains their research lab.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Successful applicants must have institutional arrangements that permit concurrent HHMI employment while retaining their academic appointment and laboratory at the host institution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Investigator responsibilities and community participation
rubrics_metrics.description: Once appointed, Investigators direct a research team, create a lab environment suited to tackling fundamental research questions, commit to mentoring and training the next generation, join an active community of HHMI scientists, and teach and play leadership roles at their host institutions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: HHMI expects appointees to lead labs, mentor trainees, participate in HHMI community events (e.g., annual scientific meetings), and engage in institutional leadership and teaching as appropriate.
